question: Assume today is 2026-09-11. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of passengers who used public transport in Spain in August 2026 (urban, interurban and special/discretionary transport combined), as it will be first reported in the provisional data of the National Statistics Institute's (INE) Passenger Transport Statistics (Estadística de Transporte de Personas).

target.what: Total passengers carried by public transport in Spain (urban, interurban, and special/discretionary transport combined), as reported in INE's Estadística de Transporte de Personas (Passenger Transport Statistics) provisional monthly data; counted as passenger journeys (boardings) across all modes an
target.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE), Estadística de Transporte de Personas
target.cadence: monthly, provisional data released roughly two months after the reference month
target.caveats: Target period is in the future relative to the 2026-09-11 cutoff, so no August 2026 data exist yet; estimate must be built from prior-year August levels, year-to-date 2026 momentum, and seasonal/calendar effects. Definitional issues: 'passengers' in this survey are passenger journeys/boardings, not

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 total will be close to August 2025 total adjusted for the 2026 year-to-date growth rate; August is a holiday month with a characteristic seasonal dip in urban/work transport offset by tourism-driven interurban and special transport. Prior August values and the 2025 monthly series anchor the level and seasonal shape.
candidates.data_to_find: INE Passenger Transport Statistics monthly totals (all modes combined) for August 2024, August 2025, and all months Jan-Jul 2026 (or latest available before cutoff), plus the same-month year-on-year growth rates. Minimum: August 2025 total and 2026 YTD growth rate.
search_hints: Estadística de Transporte de Personas INE agosto 2025 viajeros
INE passenger transport statistics Spain monthly total 2026
número viajeros transporte público España agosto serie mensual

candidates.hypothesis: Total = sum of urban + interurban + special/discretionary components; each component has its own seasonal and trend behaviour (urban flat/slightly down in August, interurban boosted by tourism, special driven by school calendar which is near zero in August). Building the total from mode components reduces reliance on a single aggregate trend.
candidates.data_to_find: INE monthly passenger totals by transport category (urbano, interurbano, especial) and by mode (metro, autobús, cercanías, ferrocarril, aéreo, marítimo) for August 2025 and recent 2026 months. Minimum: August 2025 split across the three categories.

candidates.hypothesis: August public transport demand is strongly driven by tourist arrivals and overnight stays; growth in foreign tourist arrivals and domestic trips in August 2026 relative to August 2025 implies proportional growth in interurban and special transport, which can adjust the prior-year August total.
candidates.data_to_find: INE Frontur foreign tourist arrivals and Egatur overnight stays for August 2025 and summer 2026 (latest available before cutoff), plus domestic tourism (Residentes) August figures. Minimum: August 2025 tourist arrivals and 2026 summer growth rate.

candidates.perspective: Operator-level ridership (Renfe, metro systems, EMT buses)
candidates.hypothesis: Major operators publish monthly ridership; summing the largest operators and scaling up by their historical share of the INE total gives an independent cross-check on the aggregate. August operator ridership reflects holiday schedules.
candidates.data_to_find: Renfe Cercanías/AVE/Media Distancia monthly passengers, Madrid Metro, Barcelona TMB, and major city bus operators for August 2025 and mid-2026; their combined share of the INE national total. Minimum: August 2025 operator totals and their share of INE August 2025 total.

candidates.hypothesis: August typically runs below the annual monthly average for urban/work transport but near or above average for interurban tourism transport; a stable August-to-annual or August-to-July ratio can convert a 2026 annual or July estimate into an August estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly seasonal factors: ratio of August passengers to annual monthly mean and to July, for 2023, 2024, 2025 from INE series. Minimum: August/July and August/annual ratios for 2024 and 2025.

candidates.data_to_find: August 2026 vs August 2025 weekday composition, Spanish public holidays, announced transport strikes or service changes, fare policy changes (e.g., free/reduced commuter rail passes) effective in 2026. Minimum: weekday count difference and any major fare/strike event.

directions.hypothesis: August 2026 tourism flows (FRONTUR arrivals, overnight stays) relative to August 2025 would let us adjust the interurban/special components, which are tourism-sensitive. If August 2026 arrivals growth is known, it converts the prior-year August total into a 2026 estimate via the tourism channel.
directions.data_to_find: FRONTUR international arrivals for August 2026 (or July 2026 as a proxy) and August 2025 absolute level; domestic tourism trips August 2026.

directions.hypothesis: The 2026 rail weakness (AVE -15%, MD -23%, total rail -8% in H1 2026) is a material drag on the interurban component; quantifying the rail share of interurban passengers and the August-specific rail decline would resolve whether the aggregate 2026 growth is closer to +2% (June) or lower.
directions.data_to_find: Rail share of INE interurban passengers; Renfe/CNMC August 2026 ridership or H1 2026 rail passenger levels.

methods.rationale: Anchors on the August 2025 total (362.4m, from p1's text) and applies a 2026 y/y growth factor grounded in the June 2026 rate (p113), the Jan-Apr average (p7) and the rail drag (p157). Shared dependency: a1 is derived from the same INE series as the base, so errors are correlated; the main failure mode is a tourism- or rail-driven deviation of August 2026 from the mid-year trend.

August 2025 itself grew only 2.6% (p1). A central +2.0% with a range spanning the June rate and a modest rail-drag downside is realistic.

assumptions.name: August 2026 y/y growth of total public transport passengers
assumptions.rationale: June 2026 total +2.0% (p113) and July 2026 total +1.2% (p232) bracket the recent momentum; August 2025 was +2.6% (p1). August 2026 has the same 31 days and similar weekday composition; tourism arrivals growth is expected to be modestly positive but rail weakness (p157, p231) drags interurban. Central value 1.5% with a range spanning near-flat to +3%.
assumptions.applies_when: The August 2026 calendar and fare regime resemble August 2025 (no major strike or fare shock); the INE definition of total passengers is unchanged.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large August 2026 disruption (strike, heatwave, fare change) or a tourism collapse that would push growth outside 0-3%.

assumptions.name: August 2026 y/y growth of urban transport passengers
assumptions.rationale: June 2026 urban +3.1% (p114), Jan-Apr 2026 urban +3.8% (p9); August 2025 urban +4.0% (p2). August is a holiday month with a seasonal dip in work-related urban travel, so growth is expected slightly below the spring rate.
assumptions.applies_when: Urban transport demand in August 2026 follows the 2026 trend without a fare or service shock.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp urban ridership change (e.g., a metro strike or major fare change) in August 2026.

assumptions.name: August 2026 y/y growth of interurban transport passengers
assumptions.rationale: June 2026 interurban -0.6% (p114); Jan-Apr 2026 interurban weak (p11/p238); rail weakness (p157, p231) drags the interurban component while tourism is modestly positive. August 2025 interurban was -1.4% (p160). Central value 0% with a range spanning -2% to +2%.
assumptions.applies_when: Rail weakness persists into August 2026 and tourism growth is modest.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a strong August 2026 tourism rebound or a rail recovery that would push interurban growth outside -2% to +2%.

assumptions.name: August 2026 y/y growth of special and discretionary transport passengers
assumptions.rationale: June 2026 special +3.0% (p115); Jan-Apr 2026 special +0.7% (p13); August 2025 special +11.7% (p3) was an unusually strong base. August is a low-school-activity month, so growth is expected modest.
assumptions.applies_when: Special/discretionary demand in August 2026 follows the 2026 trend.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large special-transport event (e.g., a major festival or school-calendar shift) in August 2026.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
